brief: Design an interface for a "Memory Auction House" where users bid on their own forgotten memories using emotional currency - each memory appears as a translucent, layered glass sculpture that reveals d

dominant_strengths: Clean typographic hierarchy in the side panel with confident label/meta pairing and readable weights against the dark canvas
Emotion color tokens are well-chosen and harmonize as a muted spectrum, giving each currency a recognizable identity
Restrained dark palette and consistent pill geometry establish a quiet, gallery-like baseline tone
dominant_weaknesses: The entire left ~75% of the canvas is empty — the promised translucent glass memory sculptures are completely absent, gutting the core concept
Without the auction artifacts, 'DRAG TO BID' is an instruction with no target, breaking the affordance loop and visceral payoff
Layout is a generic settings list, not an auction house; no sense of layering, bidding state, scarcity tension, or temporal urgency
fix_priorities: Render the memory sculptures as the hero — translucent stacked glass forms occupying the main stage with depth, refraction, and decay cues
Bind emotion tokens to a visible bidding mechanic: drag trails, allocation rings, current-bid ledger, time remaining
Introduce spatial composition (focal sculpture, peripheral lots, bid history strip) so the right rail feels like inventory, not the whole product
Add atmospheric typography — serif memory titles, metadata in small caps — to deepen reflective and emotional register
rationale.norman_balance: Behavioral scaffolding is partially present (clear inventory, drag hint), but visceral spectacle and reflective meaning are nearly missing because the memory objects themselves don't exist on screen.
rationale.intent_fit: It only delivers the currency sidebar of the brief; the memory auction house, glass sculptures, and bidding theater — the actual concept — are unbuilt.
